newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Foreign buying helps S.Africa bonds retrace losses.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buying helps S.Africa bonds retrace losses.

text.p: 1021 GMT - Healthy foreign buying sees noon bonds retrace morning losses after market initially hit by profit-taking in wake of sharp gains on Thursday.
Rand drifts steady on U.S. unit as local importer dollar demand matched by offshore dollar selling which prompted by keen interest in local bonds, forex traders say.
* R150 last at 14.08 percent, off morning best of 14.06 percent and from 14.10 pct close on Thursday.
* Debt traders say morning session quiet, marked by local profit-taking, but activity more hectic just before noon as foreigners take control of market.
* Local institutions still long on stock, holding back. Sentiment bullish, aided by sturdy rand in wake of forex easing, strong U.S. Treasuries and enthousiastic foreign buying.
* Next target on the downside seen at 13.90 percent.
* Rand last at 4.5255/5285 vs dollar from 4.5245/5265 late Thursday. Dealers say trade muted by U.S. Independence Day holiday.
* Concerns about falling rand gold price, which at 17-month low, not having much effect as cancelled out by good foreign interest in local bonds, which prompting dollar sales to buy rand.
